events.statement: Payment failures are real and pervasive, not a client-app illusion: payment-service logged 311 ERROR entries from 12:15:27Z to 13:58:39Z, all tied to bank-partner-api mTLS rejection (171 x 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' + 140 x 'payment <id> marked PENDING_RETRY'). This is ~8x the ~40 support tickets because multiple errors are emitted per failed transfer and only a fraction of customers file tickets.

All 311 errors share one identical signature rooted in OUR client certificate: 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z'. The expiration instant (12:15:00Z) exactly matches the metric onset step.

Onset correlation is exact: bank_api_error_rate holds steady ~0.2% through the 12:12:00Z bucket, then steps to 100.0% at 12:15:00Z and stays pinned at 100% for all 46 subsequent buckets through 13:57:00Z (min 0.19, max 100, mean 77.82). The single config change (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20:00Z, ~55 min earlier) cannot produce a 100% hard-fail that begins precisely at the cert notAfter instant; the expiry timestamp does.

Business-level success is destroyed immediately: payment_success_rate reads 99.45% at the 12:00 bucket then ~2.5% for every bucket from 12:16 onward (12:16 avg 2.55, last 2.13; min 1.44), confirming the vast majority of transfers after onset fail.

The fault is confined to the payment-service -> bank-partner-api egress edge; neighbouring services on shared components show no matching symptom. settlement-service logged only 3 WARNs (GC pause / clock drift) from 12:44:09Z, and order-service only 1 WARN (GC pause) at 12:48:21Z -- none coincident with or before 12:15:00Z and none payment-related. This argues against a shared ledger-db/kafka failure as the driver.

Interpretation: the evidence supports a PAYMENT-SERVICE-INTERNAL fault at the TLS client-credential layer (our own expired client cert), NOT a bank/gateway-side outage. The remote returned 'expired certificate (alert 45)', i.e. the bank correctly rejected our expired cert rather than the bank being down; the 100% step at exactly notAfter=12:15:00Z and the identical driver signature across all 311 errors localize the cause to payment-service's cert/secret management. No bank-side error (5xx/timeout) signature appears anywhere, unlike precedent HIST-105.

events.summary: H1 is well-grounded and the strongest hypothesis available: onset is pinned to a single bucket (12:15:00Z) by independent metrics (bank_api_error_rate 0.2%→100%, success_rate 99.7%→2.5%), the driver signature is identical across all 311 ERRORs and explicitly names our own client cert with notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, and the competing stories (bank outage, shared ledger-db/kafka, timeout config, client app) are each contradicted by at least one verified finding. However, the chain's earliest hop is unverified: no finding establishes whether the cert was actually renewed/reloaded. H1 currently rests on a log message's assertion ("expired certificate") plus a timestamp coincidence; the true origin could instead be a failed renewal job (cert-manager/secret rotation) or, worse for the ranking, an expired-cache/not-reloaded condition whose origin differs (the cert was renewed but the TLS context still served the old one — a deploy/config-reload story, i.e. different fix). This is obtainable evidence that could change the named origin, so I cannot accept yet. Confidence capped at 0.70 until renewal/reload plumbing is checked. Note also that H1's own assumption that 'no coincident bank-side change occurred' is unfalsifiable with available telemetry (bank-partner-api has no observability) — that residual must be carried as a stated assumption rather than treated as ruled out.
